episodes.196210: A surface front continued to meander near the FL-GA state line. This feature combined with a very saturated airmass and slow steering flow promoted pockets of heavy rainfall where diurnally enhanced convection developed across NE FL.
episodes.196220: A surface front lingered from near St. Augustine to Gainesville with an approaching upper level trough. The upper trough cooled temperatures aloft while high atmospheric moisture continued over the area. Convergent bands of locally heavy rainfall and isolated embedded thunderstorms developed across NE FL as onshore flow increased as high pressure wedged southward from the north and the local pressure gradient increased.

episodes.196386: Days of heavy rainfall created flooding and drainage issues across portions of Putnam County, including the Mud Lake area. This report is based on survey information from Putnam County Emergency Management.
episodes.196431: A potent shortwave trough/Mesoscale Convective Vortex tracked southeast across the area, causing showers and thunderstorms for much of the Buffalo forecast area. A few of the thunderstorms became severe with tornado and wind damage, along with rain that was heavy enough to cause Flash Flooding issues.
episodes.196547: A weak push of monsoon moisture and hot temperatures combined to fuel scattered thunderstorms over the Mojave Desert. A couple of storms produced severe weather.
episodes.196569: A shortwave crossed Wyoming and brought locally severe weather. The most notable weather was a short-duration non-supercell tornado, aka landspout, which moved through downtown Thermopolis and was captured on area security cameras. Sheet metal roofing and car windows were damaged by a combination of this circulation and debris thrown by broader thunderstorm outflow, with gusts estimated between 65 to 75 mph (EF0). Meanwhile, at the Sweetwater County airport, a 59 mph wind gust was reported.
episodes.196662: An upper level trough lingered in the region, promoting unsettled weather conditions. Additionally, a tropical wave approached, bringing plenty of moisture in the region. Widespread showers and thunderstorms were observed across Puerto Rico, with rainfall accumulations of 1 to 3 inches each day, and maximum amounts up to 5 inches. This led to several reports of mudslides, lightning, and flooding.

episodes.196980: On Saturday September 7, a monsoonal easterly wind flow weather pattern set up and thunderstorms developed across the mountains and spread across the Inland Empire. Some of these storms had very heavy rainfall and prolific lightning. The actively burning Line fire was affected and helped develop additional persistent thunderstorms. On Sunday September 8, thunderstorms were most active in the Inland Empire where flash flooding and strong winds occurred.
episodes.197033: TS Bebinca originated in the Federated States of Micronesia near Pohnpei and Kosrae as a surface trough. Bebinca gradually consolidated into a closed low-level circulation as it moved WNW past Pohnpei and Chuuk as was monitored as Invest 95W. The Joint Typhoon Warning Center (JTWC) issued its first warning on TD 14W as it sat about 200 miles SE of Guam on 10 Sep. It was briefly elevated to a 40 mph TS as it passed to the west of southern Guam early morning on the 11th. Rainfall was the more notable hazard with Guam seeing the bulk of rainfall. Heavy rains were less prevalent across the CNMI, but Saipan did see some erosion and runoff due to all the loose soil and gravel from large stretches of road work. Little wind damage was reported beyond some downed limbs and fleshier vegetations such as banana and papaya trees.

Between September 9-13th about 12 inches of rainfall fell across the Penial/Francis area (11.82 was measured at Moates Road on 9/13).  A location at 111 Penial Store Road experienced overflow from lakes in the area. This property was flooded given it's low elevation location downstream of the flooded lakes. Public works identified a crushed 36 culvert in the area of Penial Store Road and the Dinkla Road area. Water from the local lakes caused rainfall to back-up into Mud Lake and it could not drain. Impacts from this flooding event included: at Mud Lake Farm on NW corner of Mud Lake was impacted by water into the Barn/Garage (EM Verified); at 134 Karen Court flood water was in the backyard from Mud Lake and against the home (EM/Red Cross verified); a home at 111 Peniel Store Rd had possible water intrusion and the kitchen roof collapsed (unconfirmed damages, owner not present nor responsive to EM or Red Cross); a home at 116 Green Rd had minor water intrusion into the basement and water came through the floor and walls underground (EM Verified); and a garage had water into it at 263 Davis Lake Rd (EM picture confirmation). All other information and complaints have been for water near homes, next to homes, in yards, or over roads.
